doc_name: List of Presidential Medal of Freedom recipients
text: The Presidential Medal of Freedom is awarded by the President of the United States to "any person recommended to the President for award of the Medal or any person selected by the President upon his own initiative." Before 1970, honorees were either selected by the president or recommended to them by the Distinguished Civilian Service Awards Board. Typically, the medal is bestowed by the sitting president who chose the recipient, though the first recipients selected by President John F. Kennedy before his assassination were formally awarded by his successor, Lyndon B. Johnson. President Barack Obama awarded 118 medals, the most of any president, followed by President Bill Clinton with 89 recipients. Three individuals—Ellsworth Bunker, Colin Powell, and Ben Carson—are two-time recipients; Colin Powell received his second award with distinction, and Ellsworth Bunker was given both of his awards with distinction. Eight presidents have received the medal posthumously, post-presidency, or prior to being elected. In 2015, President Barack Obama stated there was no precedent to revoke the medal, referencing the award given to stand-up comedian and actor Bill Cosby, who was later convicted of multiple counts of sexual assault, though the convictions were overturned. The medal is related to but distinct from the Medal of Freedom, an earlier award given between 1945 and 1963 to honor U.S. civilian contributions to World War II. In 2022, at age 25, athlete and activist Simone Biles became the youngest person to receive the award. Bill Belichick, coach of the New England Patriots, was offered the medal by President Donald Trump, accepted it initially, but declined it after the January 6 United States Capitol attack. Country musician Dolly Parton turned down the medal twice from Donald Trump; she cited her husband’s illness for the first refusal and the COVID-19 pandemic for the second. As of 2025, 28 individuals (Ellsworth Bunker twice, totaling 29 with distinction) have been awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom with Distinction. John F. Kennedy selected 31 recipients in 1963, which were officially awarded by Lyndon B. Johnson after his assassination. Lyndon B. Johnson awarded 58 medals between 1963 and 1969, excluding the 31 selected by Kennedy. Richard Nixon awarded 28 medals between 1969 and 1974. Gerald Ford awarded 28 medals between 1974 and 1977. Jimmy Carter awarded 34 medals between 1977 and 1981. Ronald Reagan awarded 86 medals between 1981 and 1989. George H. W. Bush awarded 38 medals between 1989 and 1993. Bill Clinton awarded 89 medals between 1993 and 2001. George W. Bush awarded 82 medals between 2001 and 2009. Barack Obama awarded 118 medals between 2009 and 2017. During his first term, Donald Trump awarded 24 medals between 2017 and 2021. Joe Biden awarded 57 medals between 2022 and 2025. During his second term, Donald Trump has awarded one medal and has announced two; this number is likely to change.
